items.title: Ypsilanti Township fights U-M $1.2B computing center on 144 acres by Huron River
items.dek: University of Michigan plans a Sept. 9 town hall on its $1.2 billion computing facility backed by a $100 million state grant and Los Alamos National Laboratory partnership. The 144-acre Textile Road site in eastern Washtenaw County sits in a township of 54,000 with $36,000 per-capita income, drawing vows of continued opposition over water use, transparency and national security research.
items.findings: U-M purchased the 144-acre Textile Road parcel last year and affirmed the site Tuesday for a $1.2B facility to support university and Los Alamos national security research near power and water, per the university statement | The project received a $100M state grant approved in December 2024 and could create 200 jobs averaging $200,000 annually while positioning Michigan in AI and biomedical innovation, according to U-M and federal officials | Ypsilanti Township officials passed resolutions against the project, encouraged a year-long pause on data center project approvals through the Ypsilanti Community Utilities Authority and called the announcement a call to action, per township supervisor Brenda Stumbo and attorney Doug Winters | Township leaders learned of the final site decision by tex
items.perspective: Ypsilanti Township has opposed the project since last summer through resolutions and moratorium advocacy, while U-M considered but rejected alternative sites including state land near the American Center for Mobility. The Sept. 9 town hall in the township opens public comment on the Textile Road plan; township leaders say they will continue fighting.
